deities: Lord Shiva as Lingaraja (Harihara — syncretic Shiva-Vishnu form, svayambhu linga)

history.dynasty: Somavamsi (11th c.; later additions by Ganga rulers)
history.period: 11th century CE (worship traditions trace to the 7th c.; present structure under Somavamsi rule)
history.summary: The Lingaraja Temple in Old Town Bhubaneswar is the largest and most prominent temple of the city and the quintessence of Kalinga (Deula) architecture. Its curvilinear rekha-deula vimana rises about 55 m (180 ft) over the sanctum, fronted by the jagamohana (assembly hall), natamandira (festival hall) and bhoga-mandapa (hall of offerings), each successively taller; the walled complex holds over 100 subsidiary shrines. The self-manifested (svayambhu) Harihara linga — worshipped as Shiva yet carrying Vishnu iconography — reflects the region's shift from Shaivism to Vaishnavism under the Gangas. The deity's original shrine under a mango tree gave Bhubaneswar its epithet Ekamra Kshetra (Ekamra Purana, 13th c.). The present structure was raised in the 11th century under the Somavamsi kings (Yayati II / Jajati Keshari per sources) with later Ganga additions. Unlike most Bhubaneswar temples it is a living temple with active daily worship; non-Hindus are not allowed inside the sanctum but may view it from a platform outside. CSV town and state (Bhubaneswar, Odisha) are correct; district is Khurda.

name: Lingaraja Temple
town_description: Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, is called the 'City of Temples' and Ekamra Kshetra, with a temple-building history stretching back over two millennia. The Old Town clusters the great Kalinga temples — Lingaraja, Ananta Vasudeva, Brahmeswara, Mukteswara, Rajarani — around the sacred Bindu Sagar tank; the modern city also hosts the Dhauli Shanti Stupa and the Udayagiri-Khandagiri Jain caves nearby.
tradition: Shaivism (Harihara syncretism of Shaivism and Vaishnavism)
